The upper left side of the op-amp is the inverting input terminal “−”, and the lower left side is the non-inverting input terminal “+”. The input voltage Ui is connected to the inverting input terminal node through the left resistor R1; the feedback resistor RF is connected back from the output terminal to the inverting input terminal node, with voltage U2 marked above; the non-inverting input terminal is grounded through resistor R, with U4 marked beside it; U3 is also marked near the inverting input terminal, and U1 is marked above R1. The problem gives R1 = 1 kΩ, RF = 3 kΩ, Ui = 1 V. Reasoning: For an ideal op-amp under linear negative feedback, the non-inverting terminal is connected to ground through a resistor, so the potential of the non-inverting terminal is 0 V; the inverting terminal is virtual ground, also 0 V. The input current through R1 is I = Ui / R1 = 1 V / 1 kΩ = 1 mA. The input terminal current of an ideal op-amp is 0, so this current flows through the feedback resistor RF. The magnitude of the voltage on the feedback resistor is I RF = 1 mA × 3 kΩ = 3 V. The voltage marked on the feedback resistor RF in the figure is U2, therefore the label equal to 3 V is U2.
